newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares slip 0.15 pct in weak volume.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares slip 0.15 pct in weak volume.

text.p: Istanbul stocks traded in narrow ranges and ended barely lower on Thursday as a down correction which followed the recent steep rises continued, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed down three points, or 0.15 percent at 2,006 after moving between 1,989 and 2,019.

It has lost 1.8 percent in three-days of profit-taking after soaring 30.5 percent and hitting 10 records to Monday's all-time high close of 2,043 from June 18 when the former Islamist-led coalition government resigned.
A down correction had begun on Tuesday after the new coalition won a confidence vote in parliament on Saturday.
Daily turnover fell to a two-week low of 20.78 trillion lira ($134.6 million) from Wednesday's 24.06 trillion ($156.3 million).

Brokers said bluechip state and energy firms were almost untouched, therefore the index stayed flat today. But the short-term technical correction was not expected to produce major losses, they added.

Several brokers expect sideways trade to persist amid selective activity based on six-month profit prospects of companies because the current level of turnover is too weak to carry the index to new records.
